pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to the St Joseph’s school website. I am very proud to be the Headteacher of such a wonderful school and dedicated team of staff. St Joseph’s is a Roman Catholic School situated in the heart of Bermondsey. We are very blessed to have such an expansive, well cared for and modern school site which provides a wonderful environment in which our children learn and grow. At St Joseph’s we pride ourselves on enabling all of our children to achieve their full potential in all aspects of their education: spiritual, academic, personal, cultural, social, emotional and moral.
In our school, we aim to inspire a love of learning within all of our pupils. We strive to equip all of our pupils, with the knowledge, skills and character to effectively prepare them for the next phase of their education, for employment, to be active citizens and for wherever their lives may lead. All of our governors and staff share the same drive to achieve the very best for all our pupils. We pride ourselves on teaching a broad curriculum, achieving high standards of teaching and learning and exemplary standards of behaviour.
Our school is distinctly Catholic in its character, we aim to create a loving and caring environment which reflects the Gospel values within which all pupils can grow and learn together. The children’s spiritual education and development play a fundamental role in the life of the school and the school’s Catholic identity permeates all areas of school life. We strive to promote values of tolerance, respect and the celebration of diversity amongst all in our community.
For further information, please explore our school’s website or contact the school office by phone. We look forward to welcoming you to St Joseph’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
St Joseph’s Statement of British Values
In support of the Department for Education (DofE) document: Promoting fundamental British values as part of SMSC in schools, Departmental advice for maintained schools, November 2014.
At St Joseph’s RC Primary School, we value the diversity of the backgrounds of all pupils, families and the wider school community and strongly believe in upholding British values through all aspects of our school provision.
The DfE states that there is a need:
“To create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”.
Our school reflects British values in all that we do. We aim to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to British society and to the world and the wider world.
What is meant by British values?
Learning about British values forms a key part of children’s spiritual, moral, cultural and social education. The five British values that the Government has identified for schools to focus on are:
Democracy
The rule of law
Developing personal and social responsibility
Respect for British Institutions
How should we help our children prepare for adult life as citizens of Britain?
Develop their self-confidence and self esteem.
Encourage participation in the democratic process.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Collective Worship
Collective Worship is part of the everyday life, here at St Joseph’s. Below, is further information about the Collective Worship the children partake in at St Joseph’s. Please look at this page for regular updates on our Collective Worship.
The children attend a Liturgy Assembly, once a week, which is prepared and led by our Prayer Hero Committee.
Every week, Mrs Nicolaou delivers a Celebration Assembly for children in KS1 and KS2. In the assembly, we recognise children’s hard work and achievements for the week. It is also an opportunity to view the house points and other acclamations children may have accomplished. Parents of celebrated children are invited to attend.
Singing is an important element of the worship and gathering at St Joseph’s. The children partake in hymn practice once a week, learning a variety of hymns as an act of worship. Many of these hymns are then sung during Mass or as part of other assemblies.
Class Worship happens on a regular basis throughout the week. It is an opportunity for the children to come together to reflect and prayer on the thought given. The children have a focus / theme for their class worship.
Classes attend Mass regularly, at our local Parish, The Most Holy Trinity Dockhead. Parents and the community are welcome to attend Mass alongside the children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Ethos and Values
At St Joseph’s, we ensure that daily life, decisions and policies are shaped by Gospel Values. We build on the foundations of the children’s spiritual development. Christ and the teaching of the Catholic Church are central to school life.
Every child is provided with a rich, aspirational curriculum that inspires children’s learning and educational curiosity. This promotes a positive attitude to learning, that motivates, enthuses and develops secure foundations for life.
We also provide a strong enrichment provision that includes a wide range of extra-curricular activities to broaden children’s horizons. We empower children to make well informed choices and decisions to lead a healthy and happy life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Catholic Identity – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
Catholic Identity
Catholic Identity
At St Joseph’s our Catholic identity permeates all areas of school life. As a school we aim to grow and learn together within a loving and caring environment that reflects the Gospel values. Our Catholic identity is an integral part of everyday life here at the school. The children say prayers four times a day throughout the school day in their class; attend whole school collective worship in assembly at least once a week; attend key stage collective worship through hymn practice once a week; take part in a minimum of two hours of RE lessons every week and take parts in acts of prayer and collective worship in class.
In KS2 our classes attend Mass in our local parish, The Most Holy Trinity Dockhead half-termly and we hold special services and celebrations at key point of the Liturgical year such as Advent, Lent, Easter and St Joseph’s Day. We encourage all of our children to behave in a manner which reflects our school’s Catholic ethos and the Gospel values. This year, we have introduced a Prayer Hero Committee made up of children from KS2, whose role it is to support the teachers with evaluating and improving the spiritual life of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prayer Heroes – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
Prayer Heroes
Prayer Heroes
St Joseph’s Prayer Hero Committee was founded in July 2025. The Prayer Hero Committee plays an important role in supporting the teachers to improve the religious and spiritual education and experiences of the children at St Joseph’s. Members of the Prayer Hero Committee are role models to the other children of how to behave in a manner that reflects the Gospel Values, are there to support other and to represent pupils’ views upon how we worship and learn about our faith. The Prayer Hero Committee also have a responsibility to lead prayer and worship across the school. The children, as part of their chaplaincy, support other children when they need help.
The Prayer Hero Committee meets every two weeks to work upon developing the spiritual life of the St Joseph’s community. The aim of the Prayer Hero Committee is to improve the experiences of the children at St Joseph’s and to support the teachers in improving religious and spiritual education. They always start their meetings in prayer.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE & Sports Premium Funding – St Josephs Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE & Sports Premium Funding
What is PE and Sports Premium?
The primary PE and sport premium was introduced to improve the provision of physical education and school sport in primary schools. The allocated funding is ring fenced and can only be spent on PE and sport in primary schools.
How should the funding be used?
The PE and sport premium must be spent by schools on ‘making additional and sustainable improvements to the provision of PE and sport’ for the benefit of all pupils to encourage the development of healthy, active lifestyles. This means that the funding should be used to develop or add to the PE and sport activities that schools already offer and/or make improvements now that will benefit pupils joining the school in future years. With this in mind, schools can choose how they use the funding but they will be held accountable for how they have used the additional funding to support provision.
